subtopic: TPACK, SAMR, Dale Cone, ASSURE, & Multimedia Learning

items.definition: The conceptual framework identifying the intersection of three primary forms of knowledge required for effective technology integration: Technological Knowledge (TK), Pedagogical Knowledge (PK), and Content Knowledge (CK).
items.rationalization: True TPACK is not merely using technology as an add-on; it is the seamless orchestration of technology to make complex subject matter pedagogically accessible and engaging.

mnemonic.title: TPACK Components
mnemonic.phrase: TK + PK + CK = TPACK Harmony

items.tosCompetency: Apply the TPACK framework in designing technology-integrated instruction

items.definition: The specialized knowledge of how to teach specific subject matter using analogies, illustrations, and pedagogical strategies suited to students' learning difficulties.
items.rationalization: Shulman proved that knowing subject content (CK) and knowing generic teaching methods (PK) is insufficient; PCK is knowing the best way to teach a specific science or math concept.

mnemonic.title: Shulman's PCK
mnemonic.phrase: How to Teach Specific Subject Matter

items.tosCompetency: Apply the TPACK framework in designing technology-integrated instruction

items.definition: The understanding of how teaching and learning change when particular technologies are used, including the affordances and constraints of digital pedagogical tools.
items.rationalization: Knowing how to use online breakout rooms for cooperative learning or interactive polling apps (Mentimeter) for formative feedback is an example of TPK.

mnemonic.title: TPK Focus
mnemonic.phrase: Using Tech Tools to Support Teaching Methods

items.tosCompetency: Apply the TPACK framework in designing technology-integrated instruction

items.definition: The understanding of the reciprocal relationship between technology and content: how subject matter can be represented and transformed by the application of technology.
items.rationalization: Using dynamic geometry software (GeoGebra) to manipulate parabolic curves or digital planetariums to visualize astrophysics exemplifies TCK.

mnemonic.title: TCK Focus
mnemonic.phrase: Using Tech to Represent Content Visually

items.tosCompetency: Apply the TPACK framework in designing technology-integrated instruction

items.definition: A four-tier framework classifying educational technology integration into two levels: Enhancement (Substitution, Augmentation) and Transformation (Modification, Redefinition).
items.rationalization: Guides teachers to transition from using digital tools as simple automated typewriters toward creating revolutionary, previously inconceivable learning experiences.

mnemonic.title: SAMR Levels
mnemonic.phrase: S-A-M-R: Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate technology integration levels using the SAMR model

items.definition: The lowest SAMR tier where technology acts as a direct tool substitute with zero functional change to the learning task.
items.rationalization: Example: Reading a digital PDF version of a textbook on a tablet instead of reading the physical printed book; the learning task remains identical.

mnemonic.title: Substitution Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Direct Tool Replacement, No Functional Change

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate technology integration levels using the SAMR model

items.definition: The SAMR tier where technology acts as a direct tool substitute with functional improvements and added features that enhance efficiency.
items.rationalization: Example: Typing an essay on Google Docs using built-in spellcheck, auto-saving, and word-count counters instead of handwriting on paper.

mnemonic.title: Augmentation Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Direct Replacement with Functional Improvements

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate technology integration levels using the SAMR model

items.definition: The SAMR transformative tier where technology allows for significant task redesign, altering the nature of the learning product.
items.rationalization: Example: Students writing an essay collaboratively on Google Docs with real-time peer comments, embedding multimedia hyperlinks, and receiving instantaneous teacher feedback.

mnemonic.title: Modification Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Significant Task Redesign Through Tech

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate technology integration levels using the SAMR model

items.definition: The pinnacle SAMR transformative tier where technology allows for the creation of new, innovative learning tasks that were previously inconceivable without digital tools.
items.rationalization: Example: Students producing an interactive digital documentary with interviews conducted via video call with international scientists, published globally for public community feedback.

mnemonic.title: Redefinition Clue
mnemonic.phrase: Previously Inconceivable Learning Task

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate technology integration levels using the SAMR model

items.definition: A visual model illustrating a continuum of learning experiences ranging from concrete, multi-sensory physical experiences at the base to increasingly abstract symbols at the apex.
items.rationalization: Direct purposeful experiences form the bedrock; Dale cautioned that the cone reflects degrees of abstraction, not student age or difficulty level.

mnemonic.title: Dale's Cone Continuum
mnemonic.phrase: Concrete Base Up to Abstract Apex

items.tosCompetency: Sequence instructional media using Dale's Cone of Experience

items.term: Direct Purposeful Experiences (Base of Dale's Cone)
items.definition: Firsthand, concrete, sensory-rich learning experiences that have immediate meaning for the learner, involving doing, touching, tasting, smelling, and seeing in real life.
items.rationalization: Examples: Dissecting a real frog in a biology laboratory, cooking an actual recipe, planting crops in a garden; produces the deepest, most permanent retention.

mnemonic.title: Direct Purposeful
mnemonic.phrase: Hands-On Real-Life Physical Reality

items.tosCompetency: Sequence instructional media using Dale's Cone of Experience

items.definition: Edited copies, representations, or simulated models of reality used when the real object is too large, too small, too dangerous, or too distant to bring into the classroom.
items.rationalization: Examples: Anatomical models of the human heart, globes, cutaways, flight simulators, and planetarium dioramas.

mnemonic.title: Contrived Experiences
mnemonic.phrase: Models, Mock-ups, and Replicas of Reality

items.tosCompetency: Sequence instructional media using Dale's Cone of Experience

items.definition: The most abstract band of Dale's Cone, consisting of written text, spoken words, and mathematical numbers that bear zero physical resemblance to the objects they represent.
items.rationalization: The word 'HORSE' looks nothing like a horse; highly efficient for communication, but requires extensive prior concrete experience to be meaningful.

mnemonic.title: Verbal Symbols Apex
mnemonic.phrase: Most Abstract: Pure Words and Numbers

items.tosCompetency: Sequence instructional media using Dale's Cone of Experience

items.term: The ASSURE Model (Heinich, Molenda, Russell, Smaldino)
items.definition: A procedural instructional design guide for planning classroom lessons that integrate technology and media effectively: Analyze, State, Select, Utilize, Require, Evaluate.
items.rationalization: A teacher-centered instructional design model ensuring that technology media selection directly serves measurable learning objectives.

mnemonic.title: ASSURE Acronym
mnemonic.phrase: A-S-S-U-R-E: Analyze, State, Select, Utilize, Require, Evaluate

items.tosCompetency: Apply the ASSURE instructional design model

items.term: The 5 Ps of Utilizing Media (ASSURE Model)
items.definition: The five procedural steps teachers execute when utilizing instructional technology: Preview the materials; Prepare the materials; Prepare the environment; Prepare the learners; and Provide the learning experience.
items.rationalization: Prevents technical disasters (e.g., checking that the projector cable works and lighting is dim before class begins).

mnemonic.title: The 5 Ps of Media Use
mnemonic.phrase: Preview, Prepare materials, Prepare room, Prepare learners, Provide lesson

items.tosCompetency: Apply the ASSURE instructional design model

items.term: Flipped Classroom Model (Jonathan Bergmann and Aaron Sams)
items.definition: A blended pedagogical strategy where direct instruction and lectures are moved outside the classroom (via recorded videos and readings), and in-class time is dedicated to collaborative problem-solving, debates, and hands-on practice.
items.rationalization: Inverts Bloom's Taxonomy: lower-order remembering and understanding occur at home at the student's own pace; higher-order applying, analyzing, and creating occur in class with the teacher's coaching.

mnemonic.title: Flipped Classroom
mnemonic.phrase: Lecture at Home, Homework in Class
items: A - Active problem solving in class

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.definition: A blended learning model where students rotate on a fixed schedule among classroom learning stations, including at least one station featuring online digital learning.
items.rationalization: Typically features three stations: 1. Teacher-led small group instruction; 2. Collaborative peer project; 3. Independent adaptive online learning on tablets/computers.

mnemonic.title: Station Rotation
mnemonic.phrase: Rotate Through Teacher, Peer, and Tech Stations
items: T - Teacher-led, peer, and online pods

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.definition: Synchronous learning is real-time, simultaneous online instruction where teacher and students interact concurrently (Zoom, Google Meet); Asynchronous learning occurs self-paced without simultaneous real-time interaction (pre-recorded lectures, discussion boards).
items.rationalization: Asynchronous learning provides temporal flexibility for students with internet connectivity challenges; synchronous learning fosters immediate social presence.

mnemonic.title: Online Modalities
mnemonic.phrase: Synchronous = Same Time; Asynchronous = Anytime

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.definition: A software application or cloud platform that automates the administration, tracking, reporting, documentation, and delivery of educational courses (e.g., Moodle, Google Classroom, Canvas, Schoology).
items.rationalization: Centralizes syllabus distribution, assignment submissions, automated quiz grading, discussion forums, and gradebook management in digital classrooms.

mnemonic.title: LMS Function
mnemonic.phrase: Central Digital Hub for Classroom Management

items.tosCompetency: Utilize Learning Management Systems (LMS) and digital collaboration platforms

items.definition: Teaching, learning, and research materials in any medium (digital or physical) that reside in the public domain or have been released under an open license permitting no-cost access, use, adaptation, and redistribution.
items.rationalization: Empowers teachers under the 5R permissions: Retain, Reuse, Revise, Remix, and Redistribute educational materials without paying copyright licensing fees.

mnemonic.title: OER 5Rs
mnemonic.phrase: Retain, Reuse, Revise, Remix, Redistribute

items.tosCompetency: Select and evaluate Open Educational Resources (OER)

items.definition: The educational practice of integrating game design elements (points, badges, leaderboards, levels, challenges) into non-game academic learning environments to boost student engagement and motivation.
items.rationalization: Leverages motivational psychology through educational tools like Kahoot!, Quizizz, and Classcraft, turning formative quizzes into thrilling challenges.

mnemonic.title: Gamification Elements
mnemonic.phrase: Points, Badges, Leaderboards Drive Engagement

items.tosCompetency: Implement gamification and interactive learning technologies

items.definition: Any item, piece of equipment, software program, or product system that is used to increase, maintain, or improve the functional capabilities of persons with disabilities.
items.rationalization: Examples: Screen readers (JAWS) for blind students, speech-to-text dictation software for students with dysgraphia, alternative keyboards, and hearing aid FM systems.

mnemonic.title: Assistive Tech
mnemonic.phrase: Level the Playing Field for Learners with Disabilities

items.tosCompetency: Select and deploy assistive technologies for inclusive learning

items.definition: The application of machine learning, natural language processing, and generative algorithms to automate administrative grading, personalize adaptive tutoring, and support instructional lesson design.
items.rationalization: Enables differentiated pacing tailored to student diagnostic data, while requiring robust academic integrity guidelines regarding AI-generated assignments.

mnemonic.title: AI in Education
mnemonic.phrase: Adaptive Learning and Personalized Tutoring
items: I - Integrity and ethical use rules

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate artificial intelligence tools, prompt design, and ethical challenges in education

items.definition: The skill of designing, refining, and structuring natural language inputs (prompts) to guide Generative AI language models to produce high-quality, pedagogically sound educational outputs.
items.rationalization: Includes specifying role (e.g., 'Act as a 9th grade science teacher'), task, audience, curriculum constraints, and output format for differentiated worksheets or rubrics.

mnemonic.title: Prompt Design
mnemonic.phrase: Role, Task, Context, Constraints

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate artificial intelligence tools, prompt design, and ethical challenges in education

items.definition: The strategic program of the Department of Education providing digital hardware packages (laptops, computer tablets, smart TVs, and local servers) to public schools nationwide.
items.rationalization: Aims to bridge the digital divide between urban and remote island schools, equipping public school classrooms with 21st-century ICT infrastructure.

mnemonic.title: DCP Program
mnemonic.phrase: DepEd Computers and Tablets for Public Schools

items.tosCompetency: Analyze national educational technology programs and policies

items.definition: Cognitive principles grounded in dual-coding theory stating that people learn better from words and matching pictures than from words alone, provided extraneous cognitive load is minimized.
items.rationalization: Core principles: Multimedia Principle, Coherence Principle (remove interesting but extraneous words/music), Signaling Principle (highlight key steps), Redundancy Principle (narrate with graphics, don't read onscreen text word-for-word).

mnemonic.title: Mayer's Principles
mnemonic.phrase: Words Plus Images, Cut Extraneous Fluff

items.tosCompetency: Apply Richard Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

items.definition: The multimedia learning rule stating that people learn significantly better when extraneous, seductive words, pictures, background music, and sounds are excluded from presentations.
items.rationalization: Playing background jazz music or adding funny cartoon GIFs during a slide presentation overloads working memory and distracts from core concepts.

mnemonic.title: Coherence Principle
mnemonic.phrase: Delete Background Music and Clutter

items.tosCompetency: Apply Richard Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

items.definition: The multimedia learning principle stating that students learn better from graphics and narration than from graphics, narration, and onscreen text all presented simultaneously.
items.rationalization: Displaying text on screen while reading the identical text aloud creates visual split-attention; the eyes and ears are overwhelmed by redundant input.

mnemonic.title: Redundancy Rule
mnemonic.phrase: Narrate the Graphic, Don't Read the Screen
items: N - No identical text on screen

items.tosCompetency: Apply Richard Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

items.term: Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) in Education
items.definition: Virtual Reality immerses the user completely inside a computer-simulated 3D environment using a headset; Augmented Reality overlays interactive digital holographic images onto the real physical world.
items.rationalization: Enables simulated virtual field trips to ancient Rome, internal human organ walkthroughs, and safe chemical explosion experiments in schools without laboratory equipment.

mnemonic.title: VR vs AR
mnemonic.phrase: VR Immerses in Simulation; AR Overlays on Reality
items: AR: Digital overlay on physical room

items.tosCompetency: Integrate immersive technologies (VR, AR, simulations) in instruction

items.definition: Digital audio episodes produced for on-demand streaming and mobile listening, used in education to foster auditory comprehension, storytelling, and asynchronous debate.
items.rationalization: Allows auditory learners and commuting students to learn during transit, promoting accessible, ubiquitous educational listening.

mnemonic.title: Educational Podcasts
mnemonic.phrase: On-Demand Audio Learning on the Go

items.tosCompetency: Utilize audio-visual and multimedia tools for diverse learning styles

items.definition: The educational practice of combining traditional narrative writing with multimedia digital tools (images, voiceover narration, sound effects, music, and video clips) to communicate a personal or academic story.
items.rationalization: Cultivates multi-literacy: students synthesize written scripts, visual aesthetics, audio pacing, and technical editing in an authentic project-based learning output.

mnemonic.title: Digital Storytelling
mnemonic.phrase: Script + Voiceover + Images + Music

items.tosCompetency: Utilize audio-visual and multimedia tools for diverse learning styles

items.definition: Large interactive display boards connected to computers and projectors allowing teachers and students to write, manipulate digital objects, project simulations, and save annotated lessons in real time.
items.rationalization: Transforms passive lecture slides into active collaborative touch demonstrations, engaging kinesthetic and visual learners.

mnemonic.title: Smartboards
mnemonic.phrase: Touch-Screen Display for Active Collaboration

items.tosCompetency: Operate classroom instructional hardware and display systems

items.term: Cloud Computing and Collaborative Docs in Education
items.definition: Cloud-based collaborative platforms (Google Workspace for Education, Microsoft 365) where documents, presentations, and spreadsheets are stored on remote servers, enabling simultaneous real-time multi-user editing.
items.rationalization: Revolutionizes cooperative learning: group members co-author essays simultaneously from separate homes with version history tracking each student's individual contribution.

mnemonic.title: Cloud Collaboration
mnemonic.phrase: Edit Simultaneously from Anywhere

items.tosCompetency: Utilize Learning Management Systems (LMS) and digital collaboration platforms

items.definition: An inquiry-oriented lesson format in which most or all of the information that learners interact with comes from resources on the World Wide Web, structured into 6 components: Introduction, Task, Process, Resources, Evaluation, and Conclusion.
items.rationalization: Prevents random internet browsing; guides students toward authentic problem-solving and critical analysis using pre-vetted web resources.

mnemonic.title: WebQuest 6 Parts
mnemonic.phrase: Intro, Task, Process, Resources, Evaluation, Conclusion

items.tosCompetency: Apply WebQuest inquiry-based learning structures

items.definition: EdTech 1 refers to physical hardware and audiovisual equipment (projectors, television monitors, computers, tablets); EdTech 2 refers to software, psychological learning theories, and systematic instructional design processes.
items.rationalization: A teacher who buys expensive laptops without pedagogical training is practicing mere EdTech 1; applying cognitive principles to redesign learning experiences is EdTech 2.

mnemonic.title: EdTech 1 vs 2
mnemonic.phrase: EdTech 1 = The Machine; EdTech 2 = The Mind and Method

items.tosCompetency: Analyze foundational definitions and paradigms of educational technology

items.definition: An automated instructional program presented by a computer to achieve learning objectives, featuring drill-and-practice, interactive tutorials, simulations, or educational games.
items.rationalization: Provides immediate corrective feedback, branching pathways based on learner responses, and self-paced mastery for individualized remediation.

mnemonic.title: CAI Features
mnemonic.phrase: Automated Self-Paced Tutorials with Immediate Feedback

items.tosCompetency: Apply computer-assisted instruction (CAI) and adaptive learning tools

items.term: Formative Assessment Tech Tools (Kahoot, Quizizz, Padlet)
items.definition: Web-based interactive digital response tools that allow teachers to gather real-time formative assessment data and gauge class comprehension instantaneously.
items.rationalization: Pinpoints learning misconceptions instantly, allowing teachers to reteach confusing concepts in real time during the lesson rather than discovering gaps on final exams.

mnemonic.title: Live Polling Tools
mnemonic.phrase: Instant Real-Time Formative Check

items.tosCompetency: Implement digital formative assessment and live response systems

items.definition: Automated scoring guides integrated into learning management systems that allow criterion-referenced grading, point computation, and targeted qualitative feedback.
items.rationalization: Enhances grading transparency, eliminates arithmetic calculation errors, and enables parents and students to monitor competency mastery in real time.

mnemonic.title: Electronic Rubrics
mnemonic.phrase: Objective Scoring at the Click of a Button

items.tosCompetency: Utilize Learning Management Systems (LMS) and digital collaboration platforms

items.term: Simulation Software in Science Education (PhET Interactive)
items.definition: Free interactive, research-based science and mathematics simulations developed by the University of Colorado Boulder providing game-like exploratory environments for physics, chemistry, and biology concepts.
items.rationalization: Enables students to visualize invisible microscopic phenomena (electrons moving, wave interference, molecular bonding) through interactive visual manipulation.

mnemonic.title: PhET Simulations
mnemonic.phrase: Virtual Labs for Invisible Science Phenomena

items.tosCompetency: Select and deploy educational software and STEM simulators

items.definition: An educational approach that delivers content in small, highly focused, bite-sized learning bursts (typically 3 to 7 minutes long) designed to meet a single learning objective.
items.rationalization: Matches the shorter attention spans of digital-native learners and prevents cognitive overload in mobile and remote education.

mnemonic.title: Microlearning
mnemonic.phrase: Bite-Sized 5-Minute Targeted Modules

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.definition: Educational technologies that use artificial intelligence algorithms to dynamically orchestrate the allocation of human and digital resources to address the unique learning needs of each individual learner.
items.rationalization: If a student struggles with a fraction problem, the adaptive platform automatically generates simpler remedial exercises; once mastered, it advances to algebra without teacher intervention.

mnemonic.title: Adaptive Learning
mnemonic.phrase: AI Adjusts Difficulty to Match the Student

items.tosCompetency: Evaluate artificial intelligence tools, prompt design, and ethical challenges in education

items.term: Digital Storytelling Rubric: Voice, Imagery, Economy
items.definition: Evaluation criteria for multimodal projects measuring voiceover inflection, matching visual imagery, economy of content (not overloading slides), and emotional resonance.
items.rationalization: Ensures students are assessed on communication efficacy, aesthetic craftsmanship, and research depth rather than mere flashiness.

mnemonic.title: Digital Story Criteria
mnemonic.phrase: Voice, Visuals, Pacing, Content Economy

items.tosCompetency: Utilize audio-visual and multimedia tools for diverse learning styles

items.term: Digital Divide: Three Levels of Inequality
items.definition: The structural technology divide spanning three successive barriers: First-level divide (physical hardware/connectivity access); Second-level divide (digital literacy skills); and Third-level divide (ability to turn tech use into tangible socio-economic opportunities).
items.rationalization: Providing laptops solves only the first-level divide; effective education must tackle the second and third levels through critical digital literacy.

mnemonic.title: 3 Digital Divides
mnemonic.phrase: Level 1 (Access), Level 2 (Skills), Level 3 (Outcome)

items.tosCompetency: Analyze national educational technology programs and policies

items.term: Social Presence in Online Learning (Community of Inquiry / CoI)
items.definition: The ability of participants in an online learning community to project their personal characteristics and emotional presence, presenting themselves as 'real people' in virtual spaces.
items.rationalization: One of three core presences in the Garrison, Anderson, and Archer CoI model alongside Cognitive Presence and Teaching Presence; prevents feelings of online isolation.

mnemonic.title: CoI Three Presences
mnemonic.phrase: Teaching, Social, Cognitive Presence

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.term: Netiquette and Cyberbullying Protocols in Virtual Meetings
items.definition: Guidelines for conducting virtual video conference classes: muting microphones when not speaking, using the 'raise hand' feature, appropriate attire, respectful chat discussions, and strict bans on unauthorized recording or screenshot sharing.
items.rationalization: Protects student privacy rights under the Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) and ensures an orderly, distraction-free online learning environment.

mnemonic.title: Video Class Netiquette
mnemonic.phrase: Mute Mic, Camera Etiquette, Respect Privacy

items.tosCompetency: Operate classroom instructional hardware and display systems

items.definition: The learning impairment that occurs when learners must mentally integrate disparate sources of information (e.g., text located far away from the diagram it describes).
items.rationalization: Solved by physically integrating the explanatory labels directly next to the relevant parts of the diagram on the slide or worksheet, reducing visual scanning effort.

mnemonic.title: Split-Attention Fix
mnemonic.phrase: Place Labels Directly on the Diagram

items.tosCompetency: Apply Richard Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

items.definition: The multimedia learning principle stating that people learn significantly better from animation and spoken narration than from animation and onscreen printed text.
items.rationalization: Using voice narration uses the auditory processing channel, freeing up the visual channel to focus on watching the complex animation without visual bottleneck.

mnemonic.title: Modality Principle
mnemonic.phrase: Narrate Animations with Voice Instead of Text

items.tosCompetency: Apply Richard Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning

items.definition: A digital recording of computer screen output, often accompanied by audio voiceover narration and webcam picture-in-picture, used to demonstrate software tutorials and math steps.
items.rationalization: Tools like OBS Studio, Loom, and Screencastify allow teachers to create rapid, high-impact instructional modules for flipped learning and absent students.

mnemonic.title: Screencasting
mnemonic.phrase: Record Screen and Voice for Step-by-Step Lessons

items.tosCompetency: Utilize audio-visual and multimedia tools for diverse learning styles

items.definition: An educational paradigm where learning occurs anytime and anywhere using wireless mobile devices, sensor technologies, and cloud networks, seamlessly blending classroom and everyday life.
items.rationalization: Eliminates geographic and temporal boundaries; learners access learning modules, collaborate on shared documents, and consult mentors on smartphones 24/7.

mnemonic.title: Ubiquitous Learning
mnemonic.phrase: Anytime, Anywhere Learning via Mobile Cloud

items.tosCompetency: Design blended learning, flipped classrooms, and online modalities

items.term: Digital Citizenship: Digital Law and Copyright Infringement
items.definition: The element of digital citizenship dealing with legal rights and restrictions governing technology, criminalizing unauthorized software cracking, digital media piracy, and copyright infringement.
items.rationalization: Educates students on the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines (RA 8293) and promotes the ethical use of Open Educational Resources and licensed media.

mnemonic.title: Digital Law
mnemonic.phrase: Obey Copyright, Reject Digital Piracy

items.tosCompetency: Operate classroom instructional hardware and display systems
